evidence_quotes.quote: Más allá de los distintos subsistemas, el conjunto heterogéneo de prestatarias que sostenía la provisión de los servicios en los subsistemas satisfacía, únicamente, al 75,47 % de las viviendas en el caso del agua y al 48,65 % en las cloacas, como permiten observan los gráficos 2 y 3.
Specifically, it focuses on the institutionalization and trajectory of these services, whose course has led to the consolidation of the three existing supply subsystems within the territory.

En 1984 el gobierno provincial reconoció la relevancia que el acceso a los servicios asumía en materia de salud y prohibió el corte total del servicio por falta de pago o por infracción a las disposiciones del reglamento de obras sanitarias.

introdujo una tarifa diferencial para aquellos hogares con bajos recursos al establecer una excepción del pago del 50 % de las tasas no medidas y medidas a las personas cuyos inmuebles fuesen la vivienda de su grupo familiar

La privatización de OSBA asumió la división del territorio en áreas de negocios y la mantención en cada una de ellas del monopolio y la integración vertical, el sistema de concesión del servicio público, la existencia del sistema tarifario catastral y el régimen tarifario de consumo medido, etc.
El camino adoptado priorizó una metodología cualitativa con una aproximación narrativa que consideró el análisis de los instrumentos de política pública y los intentos de coordinación.
En el provincial, abastecido por ABSA, el 69,6 % de los hogares accedía al servicio de agua y el 41,8 % a las cloacas (gráfico 4).

Por último, la fragmentación institucional y la coexistencia de los tres subsistemas mencionados, no ha logrado que los servicios tengan una cobertura cercana a la universalización y que tenga rasgos homogéneos de calidad en todo el territorio.

criterion_notes.c1: Examines household and dwelling access to piped drinking water and sewerage services across the Province of Buenos Aires, Argentina.
criterion_notes.c2: Plain wording: YES — directly examines legal, administrative, institutional, regulatory, and governance instruments shaping water and sanitation provision in the Province of Buenos Aires (1973-2012). Narrow 2026-10-13 rule-type reading: YES (borderline macro-institutional, but satisfies scope) — analyzes utility ownership and regulatory structure directly governing service access across three jurisdictional/ownership subsystems (national public/privatized/re-statized OSN-Aguas Argentinas-AySA, provincial OSBA-Azurix/AGBA-ABSA under regulatory bodies ORAB and OCABA and Law 11.820, and local municipal, cooperative, and private providers), alongside specific statutory access, tariff, and disconnection rules (mandatory connection rules, cadastral vs metered tariff regimes, 1976 residential disconnection and property-lien authorization for arrears, 1984 prohibition on total disconnection for non-payment, Law 10.474 Art. 22 50% low-income tariff exemption, and concession expansion mandates).
criterion_notes.c3: Qualitative historical-institutional case study drawing on provincial and national legislation/decrees, institutional reports, key informant interviews (from the author's PhD dissertation), provincial public-expenditure series (1993-2009), and original cross-tabulation of 2010 National Population and Housing Census coverage data across institutional provision subsystems. Qualitative socio-legal/institutional studies are eligible even without a quantitative effect estimate.
criterion_notes.c4: Reports 2010 Census household and dwelling piped-water and sewerage coverage rates for the Province of Buenos Aires overall (75.47% of dwellings / 75.09% of households for water; 48.65% of dwellings / 47.57% of households for sewerage), disaggregated across the three institutional provision subsystems (National: 74.56% water, 41.83% sewerage; Provincial: 69.6% water, 41.8% sewerage; Local: 80.94% water, 52.07% sewerage) and selected municipalities, as well as major service continuity failures (e.g., the 2000 Bahía Blanca and Punta Alta water outage affecting over 400,000 users).
criterion_notes.c5: Population and units of analysis (Province of Buenos Aires: 135 municipalities, 15,625,084 inhabitants, and 2010 Census households/dwellings grouped into three institutional provision subsystems), exposure (utility ownership, decentralization, privatization/concession, re-statization, regulatory agencies, and tariff/disconnection rules), outcome (household/dwelling piped water and sewerage coverage), and study design (qualitative historical-institutional case study with descriptive census analysis) are all identifiable.
criterion_notes.c6: Full text is in Spanish (with English title and abstract). Per Inclusion Criterion 10, non-English/Portuguese/Dutch studies are eligible when translation from the accessible full text is feasible and the study is relevant; direct AI-assisted translation/assessment from the complete Spanish PDF full text is feasible and logged here.

study_design: Qualitative historical-institutional case study combining documentary and legal analysis, key informant interviews, public expenditure series (1993-2009), and descriptive cross-sectional analysis of 2010 Census coverage by provision subsystem.
population_and_sample: Province of Buenos Aires, Argentina (135 partidos/municipalities: 24 in Greater Buenos Aires and 111 in the provincial interior; 15,625,084 inhabitants and all enumerated households/dwellings in the 2010 National Census, organized across three provision subsystems covering 17 national, 51 provincial, and 66 local municipalities in 2010).
exposure: Utility ownership and regulatory structure governing service provision in the Province of Buenos Aires (1973-2012) — decentralization/municipalization (1979-1983), re-provincialization (Law 10.369/1985), privatization via concessions (Azurix and AGBA) and regulatory framework (Law 11.820/1996, ORAB), re-statization (ABSA, OCABA, DIPAC), fragmentation across national, provincial, and local subsystems, and statutory tariff, disconnection, and social-tariff exemption rules (1976 disconnection/lien rule, 1984 ban on total disconnection for non-payment, Law 10.474 Art. 22 50% low-income exemption).
outcome: Household and dwelling coverage/connection to piped drinking-water and sewerage networks (2010 Census overall, by institutional provision subsystem, and across municipalities), alongside qualitative accounts of service continuity failures and expansion deficits.
rationale: This Spanish-language qualitative historical-institutional case study (derived from the author's doctoral dissertation) examines the legal, regulatory, and ownership trajectory of water and sanitation services in the Province of Buenos Aires from 1973 to 2012. It satisfies all inclusion criteria: (c1) examines household and dwelling piped water and sewerage service access; (c2) examines utility ownership and regulatory structures directly governing service access across three subsystems (national, provincial, and local municipal/cooperative/private) — including decentralization, privatization concessions, re-statization, regulatory agencies (ORAB, OCABA), and statutory tariff, disconnection, and social-exemption rules — satisfying both the plain wording and the 2026-10-13 rule-type clarification; (c3) uses an identifiable qualitative case-study methodology combining documentary/legal analysis, key informant interviews, public spending data (1993-2009), and 2010 Census data; (c4) reports household and dwelling piped-water and sewerage coverage outcomes overall and disaggregated by institutional subsystem; (c5) clearly identifies population, unit of analysis, exposure, outcome, and study design; and (c6) is in Spanish with full text accessible and feasible to translate per Criterion 10. Confidence is medium because the analysis operates primarily at the provincial/subsystem level with descriptive census comparisons rather than isolating a single household-level rule.
